STUDY HABITS · 5 MIN READ

A revision plan that fits your real week.

Turn an overwhelming list of topics into a manageable set of next steps.

Start with what is actually ahead.

Write down the subjects you study and the assessments you are preparing for. Add dates when you know them. If a date is uncertain, label it uncertain rather than building the whole plan around it.

Make topics small enough to practise.

“Revise chemistry” is hard to act on. “Balance five equations, then check the method” is clearer. Break each subject into tasks with a visible finish.

Leave room for feedback.

A plan should include time to check your work. Note the mistake, identify the missing idea, and choose a follow-up question. Ask for help when you cannot explain why the correction works.

Keep the plan realistic.

Start with the time you can actually protect around school, meals, family, and rest. Leave spare space for homework or topics that take longer than expected. A missed session is a reason to adjust, not abandon, the plan.

Review the next step.

At the end of the week, ask which topics became clearer and which still need attention. Carry unfinished tasks forward intentionally. Use that information to choose what you and your tutor work on next.
